SMTO-SKL-0134 — Slack refused the request for a reason SMTO doesn't recognize

GUID: 66e4861f-4b5d-53c2-b3b5-0f2cb63bfdff
Slug: slack-provider-error
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack said the request failed but gave a reason SMTO doesn't recognize, so SMTO can't tell you exactly what went wrong.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you asked SMTO to post, edit, delete or upload something, check in Slack whether it already happened. SMTO can't be sure what Slack did, so checking first avoids doing it twice.
  2. Check in Slack that the channel, message or file still exists and that your connected account can open it. Unrecognized Slack refusals are often about access or items that have gone.
  3. If it didn't happen, ask the Agent for your request one more time. One more try shows whether the refusal was temporary.

What success looks like

  • The request completes, or you've confirmed in Slack what happened.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with what you asked for and when, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep repeating a change that keeps failing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack returned ok=false with an error reason that SMTO's Slack client does not map to a specific error code.

What this means

  • Slack returns ok=false with an unrecognized or missing provider error reason. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack returns ok=false with an unrecognized or missing provider error reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe request identifiers and status rather than inferring missing scopes or an outage.

How to fix it

  • Slack's raw reason is not kept; reproduce the same method with the same principal against Slack's Web API (or check the Slack app's logs) to identify it, and add a mapping in PROVIDER_ERRORS (skills/slack/errors.py) if it recurs. Check the target's state in Slack before repeating any write.
  • Preserve the request evidence and inspect the actual provider condition; reconcile writes before any repetition.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The concrete provider condition is identified before another deliberate operation.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
